update.headline: Inflation re-accelerated at the headline level while activity data firmed; markets traded a higher-rate, stronger-dollar mix with narrow technology leadership and weakness in cyclicals, duration, credit, and gold.
update.economy: The data mix was stagflation-sensitive on inflation but not recessionary on activity. CPI y/y rose to 3.71%, up 0.17 pp, and CPI m/m rose to 0.40%, up 0.33 pp. PCE y/y rose to 3.42%, up 0.06 pp, and PCE m/m rose to 0.31%, up 0.26 pp. Core was more mixed: Core CPI y/y eased to 2.76%, down 0.03 pp, but Core CPI m/m rose to 0.29%, up 0.07 pp; Core PCE y/y rose to 3.01%, up 0.03 pp, and Core PCE m/m rose to 0.25%, up 0.12 pp. Labor and production did not validate a sharp growth slowdown: unemployment was unchanged at 4.10%, payrolls y/y improved to 0.38%, up 0.15 pp, and industrial production y/y improved to 1.42%, up 0.29 pp. Consensus and surprise data are unavailable for all releases. Data gaps: none. Model note: none.
update.asset_classes: Equities reflected narrow leadership rather than broad risk-on. SPY fell -0.21% on the day and -0.33% over 1 month, while QQQ rose 0.25% on the day and 3.32% over 1 month; XLK was the clear leader at 0.64% on the day and 5.08% over 1 month. Cyclicals and defensives outside technology were weak: XLF fell -1.13% on the day and -7.14% over 1 month, XLI fell -1.27% and -4.40%, XLY fell -0.28% and -6.44%, and XLV fell -1.35% and -0.87%. Rates price action matched the hotter headline inflation and firmer activity tone: DGS10 rose 2.00 bp on the day, 30.00 bp over 1 week, and 53.00 bp over 1 month, while DGS2 fell -3.00 bp on the day but remains up 18.00 bp over 1 week and 55.00 bp over 1 month. Duration remained under pressure, with TLT down -0.58% on the day and -5.38% over 1 month, and IEF down -0.16% and -3.35%. Credit also softened, with LQD down -0.22% on the day and -3.39% over 1 month, and HYG down -0.19% and -2.73%. Commodities diverged: oil bounced, with CL_F up 1.98% on the day and 2.21% over 1 month, while USO was up 1.61% on the day and 8.95% over 1 month; gold stayed under pressure from real-rate/dollar stress, with GLD down -0.54% on the day and -6.75% over 1 month, while GC_F was up 0.11% on the day but down -4.67% over 1 month. FX confirmed dollar strength: EURUSD fell -0.42% on the day and -2.61% over 1 month, GBPUSD fell -0.10% and -2.19%, AUDUSD fell -0.64% and -2.84%, and USDCAD rose 0.10% and 2.46%. USDJPY rose 0.62% on the day but is still down -1.14% over 1 month, the main dollar-strength exception on the longer window.
update.predictions_changed: Both promoted model updates changed the regime probabilities. The growth model was promoted from 82.61% to 91.16%, consistent with unchanged unemployment at 4.10%, stronger payrolls y/y at 0.38%, and stronger industrial production y/y at 1.42%. The inflation model was promoted from 86.94% to 25.58%; despite hotter headline CPI and PCE, the promoted update lowers the inflation-regime probability, likely reflecting the broader input mix including Core CPI y/y easing to 2.76%. No model gate was marked kept, so there is no unchanged forecast to report.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Still active and sharper today. QQQ rose 0.25% on the day while SPY fell -0.21%, and XLK rose 0.64% versus XLF at -1.13%, XLI at -1.27%, XLY at -0.28%, and XLV at -1.35%. Over 1 month, XLK is up 5.08% while XLF is down -7.14%, XLI is down -4.40%, and XLY is down -6.44%, so equity risk appetite remains concentrated in technology rather than broad cyclical participation.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Still active. DGS10 is up 53.00 bp over 1 month and DGS2 is up 55.00 bp over 1 month, with TLT down -5.38%, IEF down -3.35%, LQD down -3.39%, HYG down -2.73%, and GLD down -6.75% over the same window. FX confirms the stronger-dollar impulse, with EURUSD down -2.61%, GBPUSD down -2.19%, AUDUSD down -2.84%, and USDCAD up 2.46% over 1 month; USDJPY down -1.14% over 1 month remains the exception.

sector_reads.text: Energy is in a short-term pullback inside a strong long-term uptrend. XLE is down -1.39% over 1 week and -3.27% over 1 month, with -2.94 pp relative 1-month performance, but it is up 17.15% over 3 months and 40.10% over 12 months, with 23.95 pp relative 12-month performance. This still looks like consolidation, not a reversal, helped by oil’s positive 1-month tone in USO at 8.95% and CL_F at 2.21%.

Financials remain weak. XLF is down -2.09% over 1 week, -7.14% over 1 month, and -2.17% over 3 months, with -6.81 pp relative 1-month performance. The 12-month return is only 0.21% and relative 12-month performance is -15.94 pp, so the long-term profile is range-bound; this is renewed downside pressure within a weak range, not a pullback inside leadership.

Industrials are close to a trend break but not yet a confirmed reversal. XLI is down -1.83% over 1 week, -4.40% over 1 month, and -8.69% over 3 months, with -4.07 pp relative 1-month performance. It remains up 10.35% over 12 months, but relative 12-month performance is -5.80 pp and the long-term label is uptrend, fading. The move still reads as a deepening pullback rather than a completed reversal.

Health care is consolidating inside an uptrend. XLV is down -0.23% over 1 week and -0.87% over 1 month, with -0.54 pp relative 1-month performance, but it is up 5.97% over 3 months, 15.82% over 6 months, and 26.00% over 12 months, with 9.85 pp relative 12-month performance. The short-term flat/down action looks like digestion, not reversal.

Technology remains the market’s leadership sector. XLK is up 0.21% over 1 week, 5.08% over 1 month, 5.58% over 3 months, 47.64% over 6 months, and 40.37% over 12 months, with 5.41 pp relative 1-month performance and 24.22 pp relative 12-month performance. The short-term label is up, fading, so this is moderation within leadership, not a reversal.

Consumer discretionary weakness is continuation, not a pullback. XLY is down -1.64% over 1 week, -6.44% over 1 month, and -7.63% over 3 months, with -6.11 pp relative 1-month performance. It is also down -8.84% over 12 months with -24.99 pp relative 12-month performance, confirming the long-term downtrend.
